newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Feb 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Feb 28.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5649. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- Ruling and opposition party talks over a joint proposal for revising the new labour law remained in a deadlock with one day left before the law goes into effect on March 1.
- The National Statistical Office reported on Thursday, in 1995 one out of every two South Korean lived in a metropolitan area, while the number of Seoul citizens declined.
- A North Korean woman in her 20s, crossed the Demilitarized Zone separating North and South Korea on Thursday morning and is presently under investigation, the Defense Ministry said.
- The Korean Confederation of Trade Unions on Thursday said they would call for partial strikes on Friday from 1.00 p.m.- 5.00 p.m. (0400-0800 GMT). The public sector, however, would not be affected.
